facts.label: Contrary evidence and what would change the view
facts.text: The strongest evidence against a Medium governance rating and a creditor-aligned policy is the 2024 buyback of USD 3,124 million that exceeded operating cash flow and was partly funded by net debt proceeds, together with a securities class action and five derivative suits over 2025 guidance and a different principal accounting officer signing the first quarterly report of 2026 than the annual report. A documented resumption of share repurchases or other distributions while leverage is above its 2024 level, an adverse ruling or large reserve in the securities litigation, or an explanation of the officer change that points to reporting problems would move the rating to High. Evidence that would move it to Low is a proxy statement showing independent oversight and no controlling holder, plus covenants in the executed documents that restrict distributions while debt is reduced. facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: - Revenue visibility is the weakest part of the credit, because revenue is flat in 2026 while decisions outside Centene's control are already removing premium for 2027 and 2028. Premium and service revenues guided to USD 173.0 billion to USD 177.0 billion for 2026 imply a change of negative 0.91% to 1.39% against 2025, but Marketplace membership has fallen 38.58% since year end 2025, the Florida children's medical services contract ended in September 2026, the Hawaii and California Medi-Cal transitions start on January 1, 2027, Health Net is leaving commercial group business in 2027 and the share of Medicare Advantage members in plans rated three and a half stars or higher dropped to about 42% from about 60%, which reaches 2028 revenue. Earnings therefore have to come from margin, not growth. facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: - Liquidity is large in total but thin at the parent, which depends on subsidiary dividends. Only USD 376 million of cash sits outside regulated subsidiaries and USD 175 million of it is available for general corporate use, so parent liquidity with the undrawn revolver is USD 4,175 million, or 26.86% of total debt. Regulated subsidiaries held statutory capital and surplus of USD 19.7 billion against a required USD 11.3 billion at the end of 2025, an excess of about USD 8.4 billion, and net dividends after capital contributions were about USD 1.2 billion in 2025 and about USD 1.1 billion in the nine months of 2026, which covers cash interest, but only about USD 20 million of net dividends is expected for the rest of 2026. Net debt is negative USD 5,158 million at September 30, 2026 and negative USD 5,157 million after the redemption of the remaining 2027 notes in October 2026; a pro forma cash figure is not established. facts.label: Contrary evidence and what would change the view
facts.text: The strongest evidence against a cautious view is that total debt is falling and the 2025 loss was largely non-cash. facts.label: Company description and ownership
facts.text: Centene is a government-programs managed care insurer that operates through regulated health plan subsidiaries, which means cash is generated in entities whose dividends and capital are restricted. Premium is set by states and the federal government, so revenue depends on contract awards, rate setting and rule changes rather than on pricing power, while the holding company relies on subsidiary dividends and its own revolver for debt service. No controlling shareholder or sponsor is disclosed and governance risk is rated Medium by Business & governance, so creditors rely on the operating company and cannot look to a parent for support. facts.label: Revenue drivers and pricing power
facts.text: Revenue is regulated, recurring and concentrated in government payers. Premium and service revenues grew 19.98% in 2025, helped by 26% Marketplace membership growth and Medicare drug plan growth, and only 3.30% in the nine months of 2026, because rate increases and drug plan growth offset Marketplace and Medicaid membership losses. States and the federal government set rates and award contracts, so pricing follows acuity data and procurement outcomes, and the 2027 changes in California, Hawaii and commercial group, the unresolved Georgia and Texas protests and the Arizona long term care rebid, with an award expected in early 2027, make the contract base less predictable than the 2026 guidance suggests. Medicaid contracts with Florida and New York each supplied about 10% or more of Medicaid premium revenues in 2025, so state outcomes matter more than the number of states suggests, although no customer exceeded 10% of total revenues. Illinois was renewed from January 2027 and several dual-eligible contracts started in 2026, which partly offsets the losses. facts.text: Medical costs are variable and driven by acuity and utilisation, so margin resilience depends on matching rates to costs. In 2025 the health benefits ratio rose to 91.9% from 88.3% because of lower Marketplace risk adjustment revenue, higher Marketplace costs, drug plan program changes and higher Medicaid behavioural health, home health and high-cost drug costs, which cut derived EBITDA before impairment to USD 2,536 million in 2025 from USD 6,200 million in 2024. facts.label: Industry forces and policy
facts.text: Buyer power rests with governments. States and the federal programs set rates, award or withdraw contracts and set Star ratings, so Centene faces concentrated buyers and a loss of a contract removes premium without negotiation, as the Florida and Hawaii outcomes show. Rivalry is most visible in Marketplace, where corrective pricing covered 95% of membership and the market contracted, and in Medicaid procurement, where protests are the contest mechanism. Providers and the pharmacy benefit manager are the main suppliers, and the January 2024 change of pharmacy benefit manager delayed rebate receipts and cut 2024 operating cash flow. Substitution takes the form of state fee-for-service in California, and Centene is also entering off-exchange employer-funded individual coverage arrangements in 13 states. citations.quote: Buyer power rests with governments. States and the federal programs set rates, award or withdraw contracts and set Star ratings, so Centene faces concentrated buyers and a loss of a contract removes premium without negotiation, as the Florida and Hawaii outcomes show. Rivalry is most visible in Marketplace, where corrective pricing covered 95% of membership and the market contracted, and in Medicaid procurement, where protests are the contest mechanism. Providers and the pharmacy benefit manager are the main suppliers, and the January 2024 change of pharmacy benefit manager delayed rebate receipts and cut 2024 operating cash flow. Substitution takes the form of state fee-for-service in California, and Centene is also entering off-exchange employer-funded individual coverage arrangements in 13 states.

facts.label: Industry forces and policy
facts.text: Political and regulatory factors are the primary credit driver. The expiry of enhanced Marketplace subsidies and the Marketplace rule raised projected morbidity, federal law adds Medicaid work requirements and more frequent redeterminations that could raise morbidity largely from 2027 subject to state plans, and provider tax and state directed payment changes from 2028 may reduce federal Medicaid funding, which could raise acuity faster than rates. Economic factors matter through medical cost trend and lower interest rates, which cut investment income, and social and technology factors are not primary credit drivers on the evidence supplied. Medicare dual-eligible integration from 2030 is both an opportunity and a procurement risk. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_cnc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 29–31; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cnc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 36; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cnc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 38; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cnc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 43

facts.label: Outlook, tailwinds and headwinds
facts.text: Over the next 12 to 24 months the tailwinds are rate increases, Marketplace repricing that covered 95% of membership, drug plan growth, the retirement of the 2027 notes and cost programs, and the headwinds are the 2027 contract exits, lower Star ratings that reach 2028 revenue, Marketplace attrition and risk adjustment updates through 2027. Over three to five years the outcome depends on whether Medicaid rates keep pace with acuity after the 2027 work requirements and the 2028 funding changes, and on whether dual-eligible integration from 2030 favours Centene. Together these point to flat revenue and margin-led earnings, so deleveraging is likely to be gradual and driven by debt repurchases rather than growth. facts.label: Downside scenario
facts.text: The most plausible downside starts with a lower than expected final 2026 Marketplace risk adjustment transfer or a Medicaid acuity shift after the 2027 eligibility rules, which would lift the health benefits ratio above the 2026 range of 90.4% to 91.1%. The first operating break is a negative gross margin swing in Commercial or Medicaid while contract exits already shrink premium, and the financial effect is a fall in EBITDA that lifts leverage above 4.11x even if debt keeps falling. The USD 1,860 million of favourable claims development, which the issuer attributes to reserving under moderately adverse conditions, could also shrink if reserving normalised. Consolidated cash stays large, but only USD 175 million is freely available at the parent. Liquidity would then rest on the USD 4,000 million revolver, on regulated subsidiary dividends, which were USD 1.7 billion in the nine months of 2026, and on a pause in note and stock repurchases, and a drawn revolver would be the first observable trigger. The 2028 notes with a carrying value of USD 2,101 million would then be refinanced from a weaker earnings base. Resilience appears sufficient to avoid liquidity distress within 12 months, because the issuer states that cash, operating cash flow and the revolver cover that period. facts.label: Overall credit view
facts.text: Overall, Centene presents an adequate but not fully secure business profile supported by government-program scale, a lower debt balance and an undrawn revolver, but credit quality is constrained by shrinking 2027 revenue, narrow Medicaid margins and thin parent liquidity. Cash-flow durability appears weak to adequate because operating cash flow swings with timing and risk adjustment. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on the 2028 and later notes, market access and ratings that are not supplied. The primary downside path is a Commercial and Medicaid margin shortfall on a shrinking revenue base. Further analysis would require premium by state, executed debt documents, agency ratings and the fourth quarter results. ## Findings
### Bottom line

The seven supplied filings and results releases support a credit snapshot of Centene as at September 30, 2026, with limitations: no executed credit agreement or indenture was supplied, so creditor protections rest on the issuer's own summaries.

In October 2026 the remaining 2027 senior notes of USD 569 million were redeemed, which the latest quarterly report states only as a later event, so debt at quarter end and after it must not be blended.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_cnc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 21; EX-99.1_2026-10-27_a20261027ex991pressrelease.htm.jsonl, page 3

No agency rating, issuer EBITDA, market quote, peer set or portfolio limit appears in any source, so Financial foundation must derive earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortization from the statements, and ratings, relative-value and portfolio-fit work cannot rest on these documents.

The annual report and the later quarterly reports state three December 31, 2025 balance sheet lines differently, each by USD 22 million; the quarterly reports say only that certain 2025 amounts were reclassified, with no effect on net earnings or equity.

### Bottom line

Total debt is 4.11x last-twelve-months EBITDA derived from the statements, but most of the USD 20,700 million of cash sits in regulated subsidiaries, so net debt of negative USD 5,158 million overstates what is available to repay creditors.
Basis: calculation C10; calculation C14; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cnc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 46

Debt fell from USD 17,401 million at the end of 2025 to USD 15,542 million at September 30, 2026, mainly through senior note repurchases, and the remaining USD 569 million of the 2027 notes was redeemed in October 2026, which the quarter-end figures do not include.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_cnc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 20–21; EX-99.1_2026-10-27_a20261027ex991pressrelease.htm.jsonl, page 3
EBITDA covers cash interest 6.03x over the same twelve months; for full-year 2025 reported EBITDA is negative after a USD 7,311 million impairment, so leverage for that year is not calculable.
Basis: calculation C10; calculation C11; 10-K_2025-12-31_cnc-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 130
### Leverage and coverage

Leverage on a last-twelve-months basis is 4.11x total debt to derived EBITDA, against 2.99x at the end of 2024, and total debt is USD 1,859 million lower than at the end of 2025. EBITDA is derived from net earnings, income tax, interest expense, depreciation and amortization because Centene states no EBITDA in any source, and it includes investment and other income, which is a material earnings line. The derivation keeps the USD 513 million impairment recorded in the fourth quarter of 2025 inside the last-twelve-months figure, and removing it would give USD 4,295 million of EBITDA and 3.62x leverage, which is an analyst judgement and not used in the checked ratios.
Basis: calculation C10; calculation C12; calculation C13; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cnc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 9

Cash interest cover is 6.03x on last-twelve-months cash interest of USD 627 million, against 9.01x in 2024. The cover uses interest paid from the cash flow statement; interest expense in the income statement was USD 678 million for 2025 against USD 647 million paid.
Basis: calculation C11; 10-K_2025-12-31_cnc-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 130; 10-K_2025-12-31_cnc-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 132
### Cash-flow quality and funding float

Operating cash flow is USD 4,287 million for the nine months of 2026 against USD 4,651 million a year earlier, and it swings with the timing of pass-through payments and claims. Medical claims liabilities of USD 21,495 million at September 30, 2026 fund operations without interest and are a working-capital float that rose from USD 20,544 million at the end of 2025, with days in claims payable of 48 against 46 at year end. A fall in that float would absorb cash that the consolidated balance sheet shows as available.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_cnc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 11; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cnc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 8; EX-99.1_2026-10-27_a20261027ex991pressrelease.htm.jsonl, page 14

In March 2026 Centene sold a USD 1,000 million participating interest in 2025 plan year Part D receivables for net cash of USD 970 million and used the proceeds toward redeeming 2027 notes, so part of the debt reduction was funded by a sale of receivables that is not in the debt figure.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_cnc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 48; EX-99.1_2026-04-28_a20260428ex991pressrelease.htm.jsonl, page 4
### Liquidity and parent-level resources

Consolidated cash and cash equivalents are USD 20,700 million at September 30, 2026, but unregulated cash is only USD 376 million, of which USD 175 million is available for general corporate use, so about USD 20,324 million is held by regulated subsidiaries that face dividend and capital limits. The revolving credit facility of USD 4,000 million is undrawn and matures in March 2030, and letters of credit of USD 113 million sit outside it.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_cnc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 46–47; calculation C14; calculation C16
### Data quality, definitions and subsequent events

Three December 31, 2025 balance sheet lines differ between the annual report and the 2026 reports by USD 22 million each, and the year-end figures here use the annual report column. Cash in the balance sheet is USD 69 million below cash including restricted cash at year end 2025, and the cash flow statement closing balances are not tied to opening cash plus net change because of cash reclassified to held for sale.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_cnc-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 129; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cnc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 8; 10-K_2025-12-31_cnc-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 132; calculation C15

- Reported EBITDA for FY2025 is negative after a USD 7,311 million impairment, so total debt and net debt to EBITDA are not calculable for that year; the action is to read the memo before impairment, which is an analyst judgement. Severity: Medium.

Severity: Low.

Severity: Low.

- The revolving credit commitment at December 31, 2024 is not stated in the sources, so undrawn committed facilities and liquidity to debt for FY2024 are not supplied; the action is to obtain the former credit agreement terms. Severity: Low.

- No maturity schedule is printed at September 30, 2026, so the maturity ladder and the principal reconciliation are drawn at December 31, 2025 and do not reflect 2026 repurchases of USD 1,847 million par of the 2027 and 2028 notes or the October 2026 redemption; the action is to apply only the events the sources state. Severity: Medium.

- The outstanding principal of each senior note at September 30, 2026 is not printed except the USD 569 million remaining on the 2027 notes, and the term loan principal is stated only as a rounded USD 2.0 billion against 1,963 in the debt table; the action is to obtain the indentures and the credit agreement. Severity: Low.

- The legal rank and security of the term loan and revolver and every guarantor scope are not stated, so the debt stack is not supplied; only the fair value policy calls the senior notes senior unsecured notes. The action is to obtain the executed documents. Severity: Medium.
- The issuer states no adjusted EBITDA and no add-backs, so the EBITDA bridge is not supplied. Severity: Low.

- Three December 31, 2025 balance sheet lines differ by USD 22 million between the annual report and the 2026 reports, and the quarterly reports state only a general reclassification of 2025 amounts; the annual report column is used and the difference is logged. Severity: Low.

- Quarterly columns for the first, second and third quarters and the six-month period are not tabulated, and balance sheets at March 31 and June 30, 2026 are not tabulated, so quarter-on-quarter trends are outside these tables; the action is to use the quarterly reports for quarterly earnings. Severity: Low.

- The credit agreement covenant definitions of debt and capital are not supplied, so covenant capacity is not calculated; the issuer reports debt to capital of 41.1% against a stated maximum of 0.60 to 1.00. The action is to obtain the executed credit agreement. Severity: Medium.
- The quarterly reports state no SEC filing date, only signature dates, so document dates in the sources table are signature dates. Severity: Low.

## Request

CENTENE CORP (cnc), as of 2026-11-05, credit snapshot pathway. Scope: business, ownership, governance, operating model and issuer history, with the sponsor and governance behaviour review, from the supplied filings and releases. No acquisition financing or sponsor transaction is in the sources, and no credit recommendation is made.

## Findings
### Bottom line

Centene is a large, government-dependent managed care franchise whose credit risk comes from state contract and federal rule changes rather than ownership, because no controlling shareholder is disclosed and 2026 financial policy has favoured debt reduction over distributions.

Medicaid is 52.49% and Medicare 24.34% of premium and service revenues for the nine months of 2026, and managed care membership has fallen 7.00% since year end 2025, with Marketplace membership down 38.58%, so state procurement outcomes and federal subsidy and Star ratings rules move revenue directly.
Basis: calculation K1; calculation K2; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cnc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 37–38

Directors, compensation and ownership sit in a proxy statement that was not supplied, so governance risk is rated Medium on the filings alone, and a securities class action over 2025 guidance and a change of principal accounting officer in 2026 are open questions the sources do not resolve.
### Key findings

- Revenue is concentrated in state and federal programs, and contract outcomes are moving against Centene in 2026 and 2027. Medicaid supplies 52.49% of premium and service revenues, the Florida children's medical services contract ended in September 2026, certain Hawaii Medicaid contracts were not renewed, protests in Georgia and Texas are unresolved and California moves its Medi-Cal UIS population out of managed care from January 2027, so each loss removes premium.
Basis: calculation K1; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cnc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 37

- Marketplace volume has reset, which shifts the earnings mix toward Medicaid and Medicare. Marketplace membership fell 38.58% from year end 2025 to September 30, 2026, and the commercial business has the best health benefits ratio of the three programs for the nine months at 80.9%, so commercial premium is lower while the margin mix is better.
Basis: calculation K2; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cnc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 38; EX-99.1_2026-10-27_a20261027ex991pressrelease.htm.jsonl, page 15

- Medicare Advantage Star ratings deteriorated, which lowers future premium. About 42% of Medicare Advantage members are in plans rated three and a half stars or higher in the October 2026 ratings against about 60% a year earlier, and the issuer says these ratings reach 2028 plan year revenues, so the revenue effect arrives in 2028.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_cnc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 38

- Financial policy in 2026 is creditor-aligned, but 2024 was not. Centene repurchased USD 1,847 million of par value senior notes in the nine months of 2026 and made only small stock repurchases, whereas in 2024 it repurchased USD 3,124 million of stock in a year when operating cash flow was USD 154 million and net proceeds from debt were USD 678 million, so the 2026 stance followed the 2025 loss and could reverse when earnings recover.
Basis: calculation K3; calculation K4; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cnc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 21; 10-K_2025-12-31_cnc-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 110

- Ownership gives creditors no sponsor to rely on or to fear. No controlling holder is disclosed, under one thousand holders of record held the shares in February 2026, and the proxy statement with director and ownership detail is not in the sources, so support from or extraction by a large owner cannot be assessed and the credit rests on the operating company.

- The receivable financing and divestiture programme outside the debt figure adds claims and liquidity dependence. The USD 1,000 million participating interest sold in March 2026 raised USD 970 million of cash, the purchase agreement can require Centene to repurchase sold receivables if certain events occur, and the remaining Magellan Health businesses with USD 312 million of held-for-sale assets are being sold, so liquidity depends on the CMS settlement expected in the fourth quarter of 2026 and on a sale that has not closed.
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest evidence against a Medium governance rating and a creditor-aligned policy is the 2024 buyback of USD 3,124 million that exceeded operating cash flow and was partly funded by net debt proceeds, together with a securities class action and five derivative suits over 2025 guidance and a different principal accounting officer signing the first quarterly report of 2026 than the annual report. A documented resumption of share repurchases or other distributions while leverage is above its 2024 level, an adverse ruling or large reserve in the securities litigation, or an explanation of the officer change that points to reporting problems would move the rating to High. Evidence that would move it to Low is a proxy statement showing independent oversight and no controlling holder, plus covenants in the executed documents that restrict distributions while debt is reduced.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_cnc-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 110; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cnc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 27; 10-K_2025-12-31_cnc-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 182; 10-Q_2026-03-31_cnc-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 42; calculation K3; calculation K4
### Limitations

- The proxy statement was not supplied, so the view that no controlling shareholder exists and the Medium governance rating rest on the holders-of-record count and cover data, and a disclosed large holder or board control right would change the ownership conclusion.

- No executed credit agreement or indenture was supplied, so the view that financial policy is creditor-aligned cannot be tested against the restricted payment and debt baskets, and a permissive basket would weaken it.

- The reasons for the change of principal accounting officer and the accruals for the securities and derivative litigation are not stated, so the contrary-evidence conclusion about reporting quality stays open.

- The quarterly figures are unaudited and the sale of the remaining Magellan Health businesses has no stated price or closing date, so the conclusion on the 2026 improvement in the health benefits ratio and on liquidity from disposals is provisional.
- Agency ratings, market prices and peer data were not supplied, so the business risk conclusions are not benchmarked against peers.

### Transaction summary and new debt issues

No acquisition, leveraged buyout or sponsor transaction is described in the sources, so this module has no deal to summarise. The financing events that matter to creditors are a new bank credit agreement entered into on March 5, 2025, which replaced the earlier agreement with a USD 4,000 million revolving credit facility and a USD 2,000 million term loan maturing in March 2030, and a senior note repurchase programme that retired USD 1,847 million of par value of the 2027 and 2028 notes in the nine months of 2026, followed by the redemption of the remaining USD 569 million of the 2027 notes in October 2026.

The sources show no new senior notes issued in 2025 or in the nine months of 2026, and no borrowing under the revolving credit facility at September 30, 2026. Centene also entered into a master receivable purchase agreement on February 13, 2026 with a maximum outstanding purchase amount of USD 4,250 million, sold a USD 1,000 million participating interest of 2025 plan year Part D receivables in March 2026 for USD 970 million of net cash, and agreed in December 2025 to sell the remaining Magellan Health businesses, with USD 312 million of assets held for sale at September 30, 2026. spans.text: # CP-2 handoff for CENTENE CORP
## Request

CENTENE CORP (cnc), as of 2026-11-05, credit snapshot pathway. Scope: the fundamental credit view built from the supplied annual report, three quarterly reports and three results releases, using the accepted source readiness, financial foundation and business and governance analyses. No rating, security recommendation, covenant capacity or portfolio sizing is given.
## Sources
| Source | Document | Document date | sha256 | Use |

| 10-K_2025-12-31_cnc-20251231.htm.jsonl | Annual report on Form 10-K of Centene Corporation for the year ended December 31, 2025 | 2026-02-17 | 097062d4e055a3b7fe83b7f7a6e69a627cdfc677e170580a5543c61781d7f32c | Business description, MD&A, segment and claims data, debt and credit agreement, liquidity and capital resources; the date is the signature date the document states |

| 10-Q_2026-03-31_cnc-20260331.htm.jsonl | Quarterly report on Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2026 | 2026-04-28 | 6fdb16147461b8c90a892872b86f94619262dc29b1649522f12be59d50d43010 | Corroboration of 2026 events; the date is the signature date the document states |

| 10-Q_2026-06-30_cnc-20260630.htm.jsonl | Quarterly report on Form 10-Q for the quarter ended June 30, 2026 | 2026-07-28 | 2be254120598acb867bfc89cb539dc675621975d5b2820213b11fde2ab54d522 | Corroboration of 2026 events; the date is the signature date the document states |

| 10-Q_2026-09-30_cnc-20260930.htm.jsonl | Quarterly report on Form 10-Q for the quarter ended September 30, 2026 | 2026-10-27 | cfb19f79c82250660e2e3f3fc4242fe18840a50e06dfa54c4c173df9081f0994 | Latest trends and uncertainties, results, segment margins, claims development, liquidity, regulatory capital; the date is the signature date the document states |

| EX-99.1_2026-04-28_a20260428ex991pressrelease.htm.jsonl | Exhibit 99.1 news release reporting first quarter 2026 results | 2026-04-28 | 85e525be3f7df9445c1acc49590c58f56053e97a34531af048cb7fd64ca5f94b | First quarter operating cash flow drivers and the March 2026 receivable sale |

| EX-99.1_2026-07-28_a20260728ex991pressrelease.htm.jsonl | Exhibit 99.1 news release reporting second quarter 2026 results | 2026-07-28 | ef848078ad02a5ade77bb7226070a38945f9e917a1e3e86d5abb0edd73e6d395 | Second quarter 2026 results and guidance context |

| EX-99.1_2026-10-27_a20261027ex991pressrelease.htm.jsonl | Exhibit 99.1 news release reporting third quarter 2026 results | 2026-10-27 | 916ad849ec4d38de97614bebc7921009e1fad702ea222f32804d2cf10f3a8c80 | Third quarter results, 2026 guidance, health benefits ratio by product, claims liability roll-forward |
Supplied handoffs:
| Module | Name | sha256 | Use |

| CP-0 | Source readiness | d46c0f15aab6565c030b2eb85cad35862c45697f1b8fa34ee2e98db39f333100 | Source set, authority tiers and logged gaps: no proxy statement, no executed credit agreement or indenture, no agency ratings |

| CP-1 | Financial foundation | 0cf861f2a27d330ac12c4369257eb74701e11332cba2c2906c19056bb82b4aa7 | Statements, derived EBITDA, debt, net debt, cash interest, liquidity, maturity ladder and post-balance-sheet adjustment |
| CP-1A | Business & governance | 148651f856628cda219bd645c9c79178bca28847ec6a259360d940261bd0c6e2 | Business mix, membership, contract events, governance rating, financial policy and conflicts |
## Findings
### Bottom line

Centene's credit quality is adequate but not yet secure: the 2026 earnings recovery and falling debt support creditors, but 2027 revenue is shrinking, parent-level cash is thin and leverage of 4.11x rests on nine months of recovered earnings.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation F3; calculation F4; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cnc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 46

Default risk within twelve months appears low because the USD 4,000 million revolver is undrawn, no senior note matures before July 2028 and EBITDA covers cash interest 6.03x. The risk is slower deleveraging if Marketplace, Medicaid contract and Medicare Star rating losses outrun margin gains, and if the fourth quarter proves to be a loss quarter as guidance allows.

Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation F5; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cnc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 47; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cnc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 48; EX-99.1_2026-10-27_a20261027ex991pressrelease.htm.jsonl, page 4
### Key findings

- Revenue visibility is the weakest part of the credit, because revenue is flat in 2026 while decisions outside Centene's control are already removing premium for 2027 and 2028. Premium and service revenues guided to USD 173.0 billion to USD 177.0 billion for 2026 imply a change of negative 0.91% to 1.39% against 2025, but Marketplace membership has fallen 38.58% since year end 2025, the Florida children's medical services contract ended in September 2026, the Hawaii and California Medi-Cal transitions start on January 1, 2027, Health Net is leaving commercial group business in 2027 and the share of Medicare Advantage members in plans rated three and a half stars or higher dropped to about 42% from about 60%, which reaches 2028 revenue. Earnings therefore have to come from margin, not growth.

Basis: calculation F1; calculation F2; calculation F11; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cnc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 37–38; EX-99.1_2026-10-27_a20261027ex991pressrelease.htm.jsonl, page 4; Business & governance (CP-1A)

- Margin repair is real but narrow. The nine-month health benefits ratio improved to 89.9% from 91.1%, and the improvement came from current-year costs rather than larger reserve releases, because favourable prior-year claims development was 1.41% of premium against 1.70% a year earlier. Commercial supplies 38.79% of gross margin from 20.59% of premium and service revenues, and its 2026 margin includes a USD 480 million pre-tax benefit from final 2025 risk adjustment while the 2026 transfers are still being updated through 2027, so a reversal would hit the highest-margin segment as its membership shrinks.

Basis: calculation F2; calculation F6; calculation F7; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cnc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 19; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cnc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 20; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cnc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 38; EX-99.1_2026-10-27_a20261027ex991pressrelease.htm.jsonl, page 15

- Leverage is moderate on derived EBITDA and sensitive to one-off items. Total debt of USD 15,542 million is 4.11x last-twelve-months EBITDA, which becomes 4.71x without the USD 480 million risk adjustment benefit and 3.72x after also adding back the USD 513 million impairment and USD 358 million of severance and vendor costs, an analyst judgement. The fourth quarter of 2025 contributed negative USD 1,046 million of derived EBITDA and the 2026 guidance floor allows a fourth-quarter result as low as roughly negative USD 1.69 per share, so the year-end ratio is not established.

Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation F3; calculation F4; calculation F5; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cnc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 20; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cnc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 36; EX-99.1_2026-10-27_a20261027ex991pressrelease.htm.jsonl, page 4

- Liquidity is large in total but thin at the parent, which depends on subsidiary dividends. Only USD 376 million of cash sits outside regulated subsidiaries and USD 175 million of it is available for general corporate use, so parent liquidity with the undrawn revolver is USD 4,175 million, or 26.86% of total debt. Regulated subsidiaries held statutory capital and surplus of USD 19.7 billion against a required USD 11.3 billion at the end of 2025, an excess of about USD 8.4 billion, and net dividends after capital contributions were about USD 1.2 billion in 2025 and about USD 1.1 billion in the nine months of 2026, which covers cash interest, but only about USD 20 million of net dividends is expected for the rest of 2026. Net debt is negative USD 5,158 million at September 30, 2026 and negative USD 5,157 million after the redemption of the remaining 2027 notes in October 2026; a pro forma cash figure is not established. Net debt overstates what is available to repay debt because most cash must stay in regulated subsidiaries.

Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation F8; calculation F12; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cnc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 46–48; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cnc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 49; 10-K_2025-12-31_cnc-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 113

- Cash generation is large but timing-driven, so free cash flow stability is weak. Operating cash flow was USD 154 million in 2024, USD 5,088 million in 2025, USD 4,287 million for the nine months of 2026 and negative USD 3,669 million in the third quarter on pass-through payment timing, and last-twelve-months free cash flow of USD 3,943 million includes USD 970 million from the March 2026 receivable sale, leaving USD 2,973 million or 19.13% of total debt without it.

Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation F9; 10-K_2025-12-31_cnc-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 109; EX-99.1_2026-04-28_a20260428ex991pressrelease.htm.jsonl, page 3; EX-99.1_2026-10-27_a20261027ex991pressrelease.htm.jsonl, page 3

- Refinancing risk is low through 2027 and rises from 2028 as low-coupon notes come due. After the October 2026 redemption the next senior note matures in July 2028 with a carrying value of USD 2,101 million, followed by USD 3,277 million in 2029 and USD 4,200 million in 2030 with the term loan and revolver also due in March 2030, and because the 2028 notes carry a 2.45% coupon, refinancing cost depends on market levels and ratings that are not supplied.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation F10; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cnc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 48

- Financial policy currently favours creditors but has not always. In the nine months of 2026 Centene paid USD 1,872 million to repay and repurchase debt against USD 57 million of stock repurchases, yet USD 1.8 billion of buyback authority remains and 2024 repurchases of USD 3,124 million exceeded operating cash flow of USD 154 million, so distributions could resume as earnings recover.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_cnc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 11; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cnc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 51
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest evidence against a cautious view is that total debt is falling and the 2025 loss was largely non-cash. Total debt fell USD 1,859 million in nine months, EBITDA could fall 83.42% before cash interest cover reached 1.00x, the USD 6.7 billion goodwill impairment in 2025 did not use cash, operating cash flow was USD 5,088 million that year, and the issuer raised its 2026 earnings guidance and reports a faster recovery than expected. The view would improve if the fourth quarter stays within the 2026 health benefits ratio range of 90.4% to 91.1%, final 2026 risk adjustment transfers confirm the 2026 margin, the Georgia and Texas protests succeed and Medicaid rates keep pace with acuity. It would weaken if the ratio exceeds the top of that range, if risk adjustment reverses, if the protests fail, if unregulated cash available for corporate use falls below USD 175 million or if buybacks resume while leverage is above the 2024 level of 2.99x.

Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation F9; calculation F10; EX-99.1_2026-10-27_a20261027ex991pressrelease.htm.jsonl, page 1; EX-99.1_2026-10-27_a20261027ex991pressrelease.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cnc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 37; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cnc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 38
### Limitations

- The issuer states no EBITDA and the last-twelve-months figure is derived from statement lines, so the 4.11x leverage and 6.03x cover are measures built here that may differ from a lender definition, and a different definition could move the leverage conclusion.

- The fourth quarter of 2026 is not reported and guidance gives only floors and ranges, so year-end leverage, the full-year health benefits ratio and the cash effect of the expected fourth-quarter CMS settlement of USD 2,668 million of 2025 plan year receivables and of the USD 1,000 million participating interest are not established, and the improving trend could reverse.

- Marketplace risk adjustment for 2026 is still an estimate that the issuer says will be updated through 2027, so the conclusion that Commercial margin has been repaired could be overstated by a later transfer, and the size of any change cannot be judged from the filings.

- Premium by state is disclosed only for Florida and New York, each about 10% or more of Medicaid premium revenues in 2025, so the size of the 2027 revenue loss from the Hawaii, California and commercial group exits is not quantified and the weak-visibility conclusion rests on direction rather than amount.

- Statutory capital is disclosed only as an aggregate at the end of 2025 with a risk-based capital level above 350% of the authorized control level, and entity-level dividend capacity and approvals are not supplied, so the conclusion that parent liquidity is thin cannot be tested against how much subsidiary cash is truly surplus.
### Strengths and weaknesses

Scale and program breadth are the strongest support. Centene describes itself as the largest Medicaid and Marketplace insurer and the largest stand-alone prescription drug plan provider, with Medicaid at 52.49%, Medicare at 24.34% and Commercial at 20.59% of nine-month premium and service revenues, so no single program decides debt service and gains in one can absorb losses in another, as Medicare gross margin rose USD 813 million in the nine months of 2026 while Marketplace membership shrank.
Basis: calculation F2; 10-K_2025-12-31_cnc-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 94; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cnc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 44–45

Deleveraging and liquidity access are the second support. Total debt is USD 1,859 million lower than at year end 2025, the debt-to-capital ratio is 41.1% against a stated covenant maximum of 0.60 to 1.00, the revolver is undrawn to March 2030 and the issuer states that cash, operating cash flow and the revolver are sufficient for at least 12 months, so near-term repayment risk is low even though covenant capacity is not inferred.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation F10; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cnc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 47–48

Cost discipline is the third support. The adjusted SG&A ratio fell to 7.0% from 7.3% for the nine months and capital expenditures were USD 568 million, or 13.25% of nine-month operating cash flow, so fixed spending leaves room to protect cash if revenue falls, although enterprise optimization costs of USD 358 million absorb cash first.
Basis: calculation F9; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cnc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 43; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cnc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 36; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cnc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 45

The weakest material dimension is revenue visibility, and the primary downside pathway runs through it. Contract exits, Marketplace attrition and lower Star ratings lower premium from 2027 and 2028 while Medicaid margin is only 6.44% of premium and service revenues, so there is little cushion if medical costs run ahead of rates, and the monitor is the quarterly health benefits ratio against the 2026 range and the 2027 contract awards.
Basis: calculation F2; calculation F11; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cnc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 37–38; EX-99.1_2026-10-27_a20261027ex991pressrelease.htm.jsonl, page 15

Earnings depend on risk adjustment and reserve conservatism. Commercial supplies 38.79% of gross margin on a shrinking membership base, favourable claims development of USD 1,860 million is 1.41% of premium, and the issuer attributes it to reserving under moderately adverse conditions, so a change in either would reduce margin faster than revenue.
Basis: calculation F2; calculation F6; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cnc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 19

Parent liquidity and structure visibility are weak. Cash available for general corporate use is USD 175 million against total debt of USD 15,542 million, regulated subsidiaries paid USD 1.7 billion of dividends in the nine months and received USD 623 million of capital even though their statutory capital and surplus exceeded the required minimum at the end of 2025, and the legal rank, guarantors and security of the credit facilities are not stated, so structural priority cannot be judged.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation F8; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cnc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 46; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cnc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 49; 10-K_2025-12-31_cnc-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 113

Cash flow is volatile. Operating cash flow ranged from USD 154 million to USD 5,088 million between 2024 and 2025 because of pharmacy rebate timing, risk adjustment payables and state receivables, and the third quarter of 2026 used USD 3,669 million, so free cash flow cannot be relied on to service debt in a single period.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_cnc-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 109; EX-99.1_2026-10-27_a20261027ex991pressrelease.htm.jsonl, page 3
### Company description and ownership

Centene is a government-programs managed care insurer that operates through regulated health plan subsidiaries, which means cash is generated in entities whose dividends and capital are restricted. Premium is set by states and the federal government, so revenue depends on contract awards, rate setting and rule changes rather than on pricing power, while the holding company relies on subsidiary dividends and its own revolver for debt service. No controlling shareholder or sponsor is disclosed and governance risk is rated Medium by Business & governance, so creditors rely on the operating company and cannot look to a parent for support.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_cnc-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 94; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cnc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 49
### Revenue drivers and pricing power

Revenue is regulated, recurring and concentrated in government payers. Premium and service revenues grew 19.98% in 2025, helped by 26% Marketplace membership growth and Medicare drug plan growth, and only 3.30% in the nine months of 2026, because rate increases and drug plan growth offset Marketplace and Medicaid membership losses. States and the federal government set rates and award contracts, so pricing follows acuity data and procurement outcomes, and the 2027 changes in California, Hawaii and commercial group, the unresolved Georgia and Texas protests and the Arizona long term care rebid, with an award expected in early 2027, make the contract base less predictable than the 2026 guidance suggests. Medicaid contracts with Florida and New York each supplied about 10% or more of Medicaid premium revenues in 2025, so state outcomes matter more than the number of states suggests, although no customer exceeded 10% of total revenues. Illinois was renewed from January 2027 and several dual-eligible contracts started in 2026, which partly offsets the losses.

Basis: calculation F1; calculation F13; calculation F11; 10-K_2025-12-31_cnc-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 15; 10-K_2025-12-31_cnc-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 109; 10-K_2025-12-31_cnc-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 144; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cnc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 35–37
### Cost structure and margin resilience

Medical costs are variable and driven by acuity and utilisation, so margin resilience depends on matching rates to costs. In 2025 the health benefits ratio rose to 91.9% from 88.3% because of lower Marketplace risk adjustment revenue, higher Marketplace costs, drug plan program changes and higher Medicaid behavioural health, home health and high-cost drug costs, which cut derived EBITDA before impairment to USD 2,536 million in 2025 from USD 6,200 million in 2024. In 2026 the ratio improved to 89.9% for nine months, but the third quarter was 92.7%, the same as a year earlier, and full-year guidance of 90.4% to 91.1% implies a higher ratio in the fourth quarter, which fits the issuer's note that Medicare earnings are higher early in the year and lower late in the year as cost sharing progresses.

Basis: calculation F7; calculation F3; 10-K_2025-12-31_cnc-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 107; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cnc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 36; EX-99.1_2026-10-27_a20261027ex991pressrelease.htm.jsonl, page 1; EX-99.1_2026-10-27_a20261027ex991pressrelease.htm.jsonl, page 4
### Capital intensity and cash conversion

Capital intensity is low and capital expenditures are flexible, but cash conversion is dominated by working-capital timing. Capital expenditures of USD 568 million for nine months are mainly systems and hardware, and about USD 200 million more is expected in the rest of 2026, so they take only 13.25% of operating cash flow. Operating cash flow instead moves with the timing of pass-through payments, pharmacy rebates, risk adjustment and the USD 21,495 million claims float, which means a fall in days in claims payable from 48 days would absorb cash that earnings do not replace.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation F9; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cnc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 45; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cnc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 48; 10-K_2025-12-31_cnc-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 109
### Industry forces and policy

Buyer power rests with governments. States and the federal programs set rates, award or withdraw contracts and set Star ratings, so Centene faces concentrated buyers and a loss of a contract removes premium without negotiation, as the Florida and Hawaii outcomes show. Rivalry is most visible in Marketplace, where corrective pricing covered 95% of membership and the market contracted, and in Medicaid procurement, where protests are the contest mechanism. Providers and the pharmacy benefit manager are the main suppliers, and the January 2024 change of pharmacy benefit manager delayed rebate receipts and cut 2024 operating cash flow. Substitution takes the form of state fee-for-service in California, and Centene is also entering off-exchange employer-funded individual coverage arrangements in 13 states.

Political and regulatory factors are the primary credit driver. The expiry of enhanced Marketplace subsidies and the Marketplace rule raised projected morbidity, federal law adds Medicaid work requirements and more frequent redeterminations that could raise morbidity largely from 2027 subject to state plans, and provider tax and state directed payment changes from 2028 may reduce federal Medicaid funding, which could raise acuity faster than rates. Economic factors matter through medical cost trend and lower interest rates, which cut investment income, and social and technology factors are not primary credit drivers on the evidence supplied. Medicare dual-eligible integration from 2030 is both an opportunity and a procurement risk.
### Outlook, tailwinds and headwinds

Over the next 12 to 24 months the tailwinds are rate increases, Marketplace repricing that covered 95% of membership, drug plan growth, the retirement of the 2027 notes and cost programs, and the headwinds are the 2027 contract exits, lower Star ratings that reach 2028 revenue, Marketplace attrition and risk adjustment updates through 2027. Over three to five years the outcome depends on whether Medicaid rates keep pace with acuity after the 2027 work requirements and the 2028 funding changes, and on whether dual-eligible integration from 2030 favours Centene. Together these point to flat revenue and margin-led earnings, so deleveraging is likely to be gradual and driven by debt repurchases rather than growth.
Basis: calculation F1; calculation F13; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cnc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 36–38; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cnc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 47
### Downside scenario

The most plausible downside starts with a lower than expected final 2026 Marketplace risk adjustment transfer or a Medicaid acuity shift after the 2027 eligibility rules, which would lift the health benefits ratio above the 2026 range of 90.4% to 91.1%. The first operating break is a negative gross margin swing in Commercial or Medicaid while contract exits already shrink premium, and the financial effect is a fall in EBITDA that lifts leverage above 4.11x even if debt keeps falling. The USD 1,860 million of favourable claims development, which the issuer attributes to reserving under moderately adverse conditions, could also shrink if reserving normalised. Consolidated cash stays large, but only USD 175 million is freely available at the parent. Liquidity would then rest on the USD 4,000 million revolver, on regulated subsidiary dividends, which were USD 1.7 billion in the nine months of 2026, and on a pause in note and stock repurchases, and a drawn revolver would be the first observable trigger. The 2028 notes with a carrying value of USD 2,101 million would then be refinanced from a weaker earnings base. Resilience appears sufficient to avoid liquidity distress within 12 months, because the issuer states that cash, operating cash flow and the revolver cover that period.

Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation F4; calculation F8; calculation F6; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cnc-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 19; 10-Q_2026-09-30_cnc-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 47–48; EX-99.1_2026-10-27_a20261027ex991pressrelease.htm.jsonl, page 4
### Overall credit view

Overall, Centene presents an adequate but not fully secure business profile supported by government-program scale, a lower debt balance and an undrawn revolver, but credit quality is constrained by shrinking 2027 revenue, narrow Medicaid margins and thin parent liquidity. Cash-flow durability appears weak to adequate because operating cash flow swings with timing and risk adjustment. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on the 2028 and later notes, market access and ratings that are not supplied. The primary downside path is a Commercial and Medicaid margin shortfall on a shrinking revenue base. Further analysis would require premium by state, executed debt documents, agency ratings and the fourth quarter results.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation F2; calculation F4
